issues.description: Concept: the attribute representing the count of enrolled and guest students. Problem statement (description text) names these attributes as 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents' (informal short names). The UML diagram in the problem statement and the reference implementation (solution) use the identifiers 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' (prefixed with 'numberOf'). The template file contains a TODO at the attributes location but no concrete names. A student reading the textual task could implement fields and constructor parameters using 'inscribedStudents'/'guestStudents' while the tests, UML and solution expect 'numberOfInscribedStudents'/'numberOfGuestStudents', leading to confusion about the exact field names and constructor parameter order required by tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent across artifacts. Update the problem statement text (line 17) to refer to 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' so they match the UML (lines 64-68) and the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java lines 6-10). Alternatively, if you prefer the shorter names, change the UML and all code/tests to use 'inscribedStudents' and 'guestStudents'. Prefer keeping 'numberOfInscribedStudents' and 'numberOfGuestStudents' to match existing constructor/getter naming and test expectations.
